scope: Existing upLoginData/reLoginView/refreshExplore callback transport for standalone original login actions/form login; ordered task-local UI facts through throw/cancel/close, without Keychain writes or synchronous same-source/JVM reentry.

actionSliceCoordination.author: /root/login_info_v2_review
actionSliceCoordination.authorConfirmed: First action slice adds operation loginAction with action/credentials/isLongClick/timeoutMs and result executed. It uses the same existing source actor/process/owner and explicit taskID; UI callbacks remain typed unsupported. No new state owner, VM, JSC or implicit pre-action loginInfo write.
actionSliceCoordination.integrationBoundary: The snapshots only identify the observed seam. A later frozen action manifest/canonical integration must be rebound before callback implementation or SDK selection.

conclusion: No existing channel currently carries ordered typed UI callbacks. The existing taskID/terminal envelope is a viable narrow extension point; completedEffects and source/credential state wires are not UI event payload channels. Existing unsupported errors are intentional safe boundaries, not evidence of a currently implemented callback silently succeeding.

currentPath.fact: upLoginData, reLoginView and refreshExplore throw UnsupportedRuleCapability. The same environment/source/task is already available; no callback data is currently accepted.

Per execute holds task id/session/job/deadline and linkedSet hostEffects. Effect labels are bounded to32 distinct strings/256 UTF-8 bytes; duplicate labels collapse. There is no typed ordered callback sequence or payload snapshot.

Success emits top-level completedEffects. Catch merges state/host/task effect labels, selects error code, sanitizes sensitive login message and emits completedEffects inside error. Final cleanup removes task and closes its environment. Any new callback data retained only on the transient task would disappear unless serialized before that cleanup on both success and failure.

A JNI worker synchronously calls dispatch; Swift launches asynchronous host work but blocks this worker on a semaphore until the response/deadline. Main-thread synchronous entry is explicitly refused. Timeout seals possible-effects registration, cancels host work and reports conservative labels. No ordered UI payload codec exists.

The one process owns the one runtime and persistent Host. Existing bindings grant explicit sourceURL/revision and actual state/credential/Cookie/book owners; generic state.read/state.commit or source.loginInfo cannot be reused to grant UI authority or store transient callback data.

LegadoRuntimeError/Envelope know only code/message/completedEffects. executeResponse parses Envelope first; ok=false throws before executeOriginal can call its success observer. Cancellation preserves a typed failure only when completedEffects is nonempty, otherwise checkCancellation may replace it with plain CancellationError. Unknown added JSON fields would be discarded by current decoders.

NativeLegadoOriginalPreviewExecutor observes effect labels, closes the session, checks deadline, revokes the same owner, then returns. Its catch reconstructs a RuntimeError from a sorted union of effect names. Callback payloads would need a separate carried snapshot across decode, close, cancellation and owner cleanup.

An explicit per-source gate remains held while original executor is awaited; defer release runs on return/throw. Form/UI service wrappers reconstruct sanitized errors and sorted effect unions. Source-authored actions are being moved to that same gate in the independent action slice. UI application must remain with the current form generation/owned task after this gate is released.

blockingFacts.classification: confirmed missing transport / explicitly unsupported capability
blockingFacts.detail: A String effect set cannot encode repeated update/render events, their order, nullable data or deltaUp. Putting JSON/password values into effect names would both lose semantics and leak data into diagnostic/evidence metadata.

blockingFacts.classification: confirmed structural blocker for a future naive success-DTO-only extension, not a claim of a supported callback already losing events
blockingFacts.detail: Events added only to successful loginAction DTOs never reach the caller after JVM throw, Envelope rejection, cancellation normalization, DTO decode failure, session close failure or App error reconstruction. A callback-only cancelled task with no persistent effects currently becomes plain CancellationError; future nonempty callback metadata must survive without relabeling the task success.

blockingFacts.classification: proven wait-graph hazard if a new synchronous Host handler awaits rerender; no present deadlock reproduction is claimed
waitGraph: Source service acquires its source key
Host awaits UI rerender that calls the same source service
rerender awaits the already-held source key
original execution cannot release the source key until NativeHost returns
blockingFacts.detail: A pure MainActor field update is not inherently this cycle. The prohibited edge is waiting for another source/JVM render/action from inside the synchronous Host callback. An ACK-only event capture can be safe; rendering must be scheduled after the current operation/close releases its source gate.

minimalNextConnection.recommendedSeam: Extend this already-authorized RuntimeTask terminal transport with a separate immutable bounded ordered event snapshot. Do not change NativeHost or add a registry/store merely to transport terminal callback facts unless later evidence requires live delivery.
minimalNextConnection.kotlin: OriginalSourceLoginHost -> a narrow RulePlatform/ProductionRulePlatform task-event recorder enabled only for the bound standalone login operations. Capture each callback eagerly while its source/environment/task is valid. RuntimeTask holds only request-local control data, not a VM reference, source state, live Rhino object or persistent owner.
minimalNextConnection.wire: Separate typed event kind and ordered sequence/index from completedEffects. Encode the same event snapshot on success and on typed error, including cancellation. Reserve/validate aggregate envelope budget before accepting an event so overflow fails explicitly while preserving all previously accepted events and effects. Existing4-MiB request/8-MiB result/finite envelope constraints remain; exact event caps need an explicit source-scoped contract, not invented unconstrained arrays.
minimalNextConnection.package: LegadoOriginalModels typed Codable/Sendable event DTO; RuntimeError and Envelope carry optional events without including payload in errorDescription. executeResponse and executeOriginal must preserve/observe them on false envelopes, late cancellation and DTO decoding errors. A nonempty callback list is retained even when completedEffects is empty; error code/original failure is not converted to success.
minimalNextConnection.appExecutor: Observe only immutable task-local facts in NativeLegadoOriginalPreviewExecutor. Merge/preserve the same ordered snapshot when session close/deadline/revoke processing fails. Extend the existing result/receipt/error routes rather than constructing another owner or global UI queue.
minimalNextConnection.appConsumer: After the same source service releases its gate, the existing live form/owned task consumes events sequentially with current source revision and form generation. UI disappearance or supersession prevents stale publication; retained terminal facts distinguish callback emission from actual UI application. Do not call putLoginInfo, confirm/login(), generic state.commit or Keychain from event delivery.
minimalNextConnection.timingBoundary: Terminal event delivery preserves emitted sequence through normal throw/cancel paths but defers UI scheduling until task completion. Locked Android callbacks post during action execution; do not claim scheduler/timing parity from terminal buffering. If live delivery is required, separately authorize an ACK-only task-bound Host event sink whose callback never awaits same-source/JVM work and whose timeout/sealed-registration semantics preserve acknowledged facts.
minimalNextConnection.notInThisReview: No encoding, DTO, Host, UI, harness or test definition is changed. The first action slice remains unsupported for these callbacks.

typedSemanticsToRetain: upLoginData(null) is a distinct reset-to-current-row-defaults event. Locked SourceLoginDialog.handleUpUiData(null) rebuilds the transient map from current rendered rows and defaults and drops hidden entries; it does not reload Keychain.

upLoginData(map) is not a persistent map merge: source values are nullable toString at capture; null differs from string "null" and from empty string. Known controls may use row defaults while unknown keys map null to empty. Preserve null and per-event Map iteration if listener order is observable; eager ordered entries avoid retaining live Java/Rhino objects or later map mutations.

reLoginView(false) requests the original rerender path; refreshExplore aliases that event for this host. reLoginView(true) preserves the distinct delta/reuse request and must not be silently replaced by full form replacement.
Do not deduplicate identical events or sort their payloads as effects. A sequence update(A), render(false), update(B), render(true), update(B) has five emissions even when two payloads are equal.

Programmatic select/text updates can trigger the original watchers/listeners. Those follow-up actions require the existing owned UI task/source lifecycle; callback capture itself cannot synchronously launch them into the active source/JVM invocation.
requiredNextSliceEvidence: Real JVM callback emission followed by ordinary JS throw: exact typed ordered events and original SCRIPT_ERROR plus actual prior effects survive; raw callback values never enter diagnostics.
Callback-only then cancellation/timeout: events survive even when completedEffects is empty, task is still failed/cancelled, and no false UI-applied/Keychain receipt is asserted.
Repeated mixed update/reset/render(delta) emissions preserve order and null/empty data; later mutation of the original Map cannot change an earlier captured snapshot.
Swift Package failed-envelope, successful DTO decode failure, late cancellation, native close failure and App sanitized-error reconstruction preserve the same event facts and code/effects.

A controlled Native loopback/form consumer drains cancellation and proves no synchronous same-source reentry, no stale form publication, no callback-generated credential writes, and explicit unsupported behavior for any still-unimplemented UI semantic.
nextAuthorization: Freeze this review first; root separately authorizes any concrete callback implementation. No new macro plan or producer/SDK/tag is introduced.
